security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when code reads or writes CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) / CSR_MSECCFGH (0x757) on hardware where no mseccfg-field-adding extension (Smmpm, Smepmp, Zkr, etc.) is implemented, the access silently succeeds (reads return 0, writes are ignored) under the new 'reserved' semantics, whereas the old 'optional' semantics would have caused an illegal-instruction trap. Kernel code that probes mseccfg via csr_read and branches on the absence of a trap to infer that PMM/MML/MMWP fields are operational will falsely conclude these security features exist.
security_spec.summary: mseccfg changed from optional (trap on access) to conditionally-existent with reserved fallback (read-zero/write-ignored); kernel must check extension presence (misa/DT) before interpreting mseccfg fields, because reserved reads returning 0 are indistinguishable from 'all security features off'

findings.finding: MSECCFG_PMM bit definitions are aliases for ENVCFG_PMM (pointer masking). These are compile-time constants used with CSR_ENVCFG (0x10a)/CSR_MENVCFG (0x30a), not CSR_MSECCFG (0x747). No trap-probing of mseccfg occurs. The only mseccfg bit definitions are PMM aliases; no MML, MMWP, RLB, SSEED, or USEED bits are defined.
findings.snippet:
/* mseccfg bits */
#define MSECCFG_PMM			ENVCFG_PMM
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFG=0x747 and CSR_MSECCFGH=0x757 are defined as symbolic constants but never used in any csr_read()/csr_write()/csr_set()/csr_clear() call or assembly CSR instruction anywhere in the kernel (verified by exhaustive search of arch/riscv/*.{c,h,S}). No trap-probing pattern exists.
